hero.lede: I study the gap between what generative AI systems do and what people think they are doing. My work examines what users notice, miss, trust, and disclose in real interactions with AI. I also build the research tools needed to study those interactions.
hero.context: PhD candidate in Computer Science at The George Washington University.

researchApproach: Most AI evaluations focus on model behavior. I focus on the person interacting with the model. Through interactive studies, surveys, and interviews, I examine how people interpret AI responses, recognize problems, and decide when to rely on a system. I also build the chat interfaces, auditing workflows, and privacy tools that make those studies possible.
Across this work, I ask what trustworthy AI evaluation should measure when human judgment is part of the system—not merely an observer of it.

jobSearch.text: I'm looking for research and research-engineering roles. If your team evaluates AI systems with real users — or needs the tooling to do it — I'd like to talk.

projectsPage.lede: Five projects spanning human-centered AI auditing, privacy and interaction histories, workplace governance, and the systems behind that research.

publicationsPage.lede: Peer-reviewed work on how people judge AI systems, how researchers should measure those judgments, and how privacy information is produced, maintained, and communicated.
